page: Microsoft Azure NC40ads_H100_v5 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for compute-intensive AI, machine learning, and data analytics tasks. The instance runs on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V84 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz, providing 40 dedicated physical cores without hyper-threading overhead (1 thread per core). System memory comprises 320.0 GB of RAM, offering 8.0 GB per core. For acceleration, the server is equipped with a single NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU featuring 94 GB of VRAM. It also bundles 3977 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark evaluations reflect high performance across host compute and memory subsystems. In multi-core throughput, the server scored 23,376.0 in Geekbench, placing it in the top 10%, while PassMark recorded an aggregate CPU score of 73,108.27 and an extended instruction score of 100,393.07. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 525.91 GB/sec. Memory subsystem tests demonstrated exceptional throughput, marked by a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,177.48 and cached small-block read speeds reaching 5,952.26 GB/sec. Uncached large-block reads and writes posted 182.31 GB/sec and 91.33 GB/sec, respectively.

On GPU text-generation tasks, the server delivered 286.08 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model and 33.22 tokens per second on a 7B model, ranking in the top 25%. However, scaling to a 70B parameter model dropped text generation throughput to 3.88 tokens per second, falling into the middle 50% tier. In-memory data workloads demonstrated high capacity, with Redis SET operations achieving 100.89 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance packs substantial hardware density into a single-GPU node by combining dedicated AMD EPYC cores, 320 GB of RAM, and nearly 4 TB of high-speed NVMe storage. This architecture suits workloads needing local low-latency cache and sizable host memory alongside an accelerator, including medium-scale LLM inference, computer vision pipelines, ray tracing, and large-scale data transformation.
